[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard establishes the mandatory naming convention for all Gainwell-developed AI agents deployed on the M365 Copilot platform. It defines a structured name format, segment rules, display truncation constraints, and a versioning workflow that ensures agents are discoverable, distinguishable from vendor-provided agents, and controllable through the change process defined in STD-TEC-AI-004 and STD-GOV-AI-004.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all Gainwell-developed AI agents deployed through M365 Agent Builder or Copilot Studio, at all lifecycle states (Proposed, Pilot, Production, Contained, Retired). Vendor-provided agents (Microsoft-native or third-party) are not renamed under this standard; they retain their vendor-assigned names.

OpenAI Codex is an approved Gainwell technology for development productivity use. Agent development on Codex is not the enterprise-recommended pattern; this naming standard does not apply to Codex and no Codex agent naming convention is defined under this standard.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. All agents must have a compliant name before promotion to Pilot state.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Several M365 platform constraints make an explicit naming convention necessary:

- The M365 Agent Builder platform enforces a hard maximum of 42 characters for any agent name. Names exceeding this limit are rejected at save time.
- The M365 UI navigation panel displays approximately the first 24 characters of an agent name; characters beyond that are truncated and visible only on mouseover. Names must front-load the most distinctive information.
- Once an agent is published for broad use, configuration changes must be developed and validated in a separate versioned instance before promotion. The name must make the active version distinguishable from drafts or prior versions.
- Users need to identify whether an agent is Gainwell-developed or a vendor-provided agent without opening the agent detail view.

[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Naming Pattern:**

```text
[Agent Provider] [Role Tag] [Capability] [Version]
```

All four segments are required for all Gainwell-developed agents.

**Segment Definitions:**

_Agent Provider:_

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `GW` | Gainwell-developed agent |
| *(none)* | Vendor-provided agent — do not prefix; retain the vendor's native name |

_Role Tag:_

Identifies the primary target user persona.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `PM` | Project Manager |
| `SM` | Scrum Master |
| `BA` | Business Analyst (includes Product Owner) |
| `TS` | Test Analyst |
| `EN` | Engineer or Developer |
| `AR` | Architect |
| `CF` | Configuration Analyst |

Use the role tag that best represents the primary user. If an agent legitimately serves multiple roles equally, choose the role that initiates the primary workflow and document the secondary audience in the agent's capability contract.

_Capability Name:_

Rules:
- Use title case
- 2 to 4 words preferred; 5 words maximum
- Use plain business language — avoid technical jargon, abbreviations, and acronyms unless universally understood by the target role
- The combined `[GW] [Role Tag] [Capability]` string must be 24 characters or fewer to ensure the most distinctive information — provider, role, and capability — appears within the first 24 characters of the displayed name. The version segment begins at position 25 and may be truncated in the M365 navigation panel; this is acceptable because the capability must be identifiable from the first 24 characters alone. The full agent name including version must be 42 characters or fewer to prevent platform rejection at save time.

_Version:_

Format: `v[Major].[Minor].[Patch]`

| Segment | Increment when |
|---|---|
| Major | Capability scope, persona, or output contract changes significantly |
| Minor | Prompt logic, knowledge sources, or behavior meaningfully updated |
| Patch | Typos, formatting fixes, or minor wording corrections |

**Display Truncation Validation:**

Before any promotion, run both checks:

1. **Platform limit check (hard constraint):** Count the total characters in the full agent name including spaces. The name must be 42 characters or fewer. Names exceeding this limit are rejected by the M365 platform at save time.

2. **Display truncation check (readability):** Count the first 24 characters of the full agent name. Confirm the truncated string alone identifies provider, role, and a recognizable capability fragment. If the truncated string is ambiguous or duplicates another agent of a different capability's first 24 characters, shorten the capability name.

**Well-Formed Examples:**

| Agent Name | Provider | Role | Capability | Version |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GW PM Daily Briefing v1.0.0` | GW | PM | Daily Briefing | v1.0.0 |
| `GW PM Meeting Intel v1.2.1` | GW | PM | Meeting Intel | v1.2.1 |
| `GW BA Req Organizer v1.0.0` | GW | BA | Req Organizer | v1.0.0 |
| `GW EN Code Reviewer v2.0.0` | GW | EN | Code Reviewer | v2.0.0 |

[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#mandatory-versioning-workflow]

### Mandatory Versioning Workflow

1. Never make prompt or configuration changes directly to a Production agent
2. Clone the agent and increment the version in the name before making any changes
3. Test the new versioned instance through the Pilot lifecycle state
4. On governance approval, promote the new version to Production
5. Retire or archive the prior version per STD-GOV-AI-005
6. Update the agent's change log entry per STD-TEC-AI-004 and STD-GOV-AI-004
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Review the role tag list at least quarterly to confirm it covers all primary personas active in the enterprise AI portfolio
- Validate all Production agent names against this pattern during the monthly metadata currency check (STD-TEC-AI-001)
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Gainwell-developed agents must not be published without the full four-segment naming pattern
- Version must not be omitted from the name to save characters — abbreviate the capability name instead
- The same first 24 characters must not appear in two agents of different capabilities; versioned instances of the same capability temporarily co-existing during the clone-and-version promotion workflow are exempt from this rule
page_texts.13:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Requests to use an unapproved role tag require architecture board approval with a description of the new persona and a proposed controlled value
2. Requests to exceed the 42-character limit are not possible to approve — the platform enforces this limit at save time

[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#quality-gates]

#### Quality Gates

An agent name must pass all of the following checks before promotion to Pilot or Production:

1. Follows the `[GW] [Role Tag] [Capability] [Version]` pattern
2. Role tag value is from the approved list above
3. Version follows `v[Major].[Minor].[Patch]` format
4. Total name length is 42 characters or fewer (platform hard limit)
5. First 24 characters are meaningful and unambiguous
6. No duplication of an existing agent's first 24 characters in the capability registry; versioned instances of the same capability undergoing the clone-and-version workflow are exempt
7. Capability name uses plain business language with no unexplained acronyms or abbreviations
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#platform-character-limit-note]

#### Platform Character Limit Note

The 42-character limit is enforced by the M365 Agent Builder platform at save time — it is not a preference but a hard platform constraint. All naming decisions must account for this limit before build begins, not after.

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#phase-1-name-design-before-build]

#### Phase 1: Name Design (Before Build)

1. Draft the candidate name using the four-segment pattern
2. Run both validation checks (platform limit and display truncation) against the draft name
3. Verify that no existing agent of a different capability in the capability registry has the same first 24 characters; versioned instances of the same capability under the clone-and-version workflow are exempt
4. Register the candidate name in the capability registry before build begins to prevent duplicate naming during parallel builds
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#phase-2-version-lifecycle-management]

#### Phase 2: Version Lifecycle Management

1. At each behavioral change, increment the correct version segment per the version increment rules
2. Clone and version before changing — never edit a Production agent directly
3. Record the version increment in the Change Log per STD-TEC-AI-004

[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Pattern compliance | Name follows `[GW] [Role Tag] [Capability] [Version]` | Pattern match check | Name validation record |
| Platform limit | Name is 42 characters or fewer | Character count | Character count verification |
| Display truncation | First 24 characters are unambiguous and do not duplicate an agent of a different capability; versioned instances of the same capability during rollout are exempt | Registry comparison | Registry duplicate check |
| Version format | Version follows `v[Major].[Minor].[Patch]` | Format validation | Version format check |

---
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-007-ai-agent-naming-convention.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Name does not follow pattern: block promotion; return for rename before re-review
- Name exceeds 42 characters: blocked by the platform at save time; shorten the **capability name only** before retrying — the version must not be abbreviated (see Prohibited Practices)
- Duplicate first-24-character string: block promotion; resolve naming conflict before re-review
- Version not incremented from prior published version: block promotion; require version bump and change log entry
